summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, bipolar disorder, and GERD was admitted for a four-day history of abdominal pain radiating to the left flank, nausea, vomiting, and hematemesis. His symptoms were consistent with a flare of chronic pancreatitis, and he was managed with bowel rest, intravenous hydration, and IV pain control. A small amount of blood in his vomitus was attributed to a likely Mallory-Weiss tear, with no hemodynamic instability. Flank pain resolved, urinalysis was negative, and no imaging was performed. He gradually advanced to a regular diet, transitioned to oral pain medication, and had stable vital signs and labs. He was discharged home on his prior medications, including metformin, with instructions to maintain a low-fat diet, avoid alcohol, and follow up with his primary care physician.
